I'm 54 this year, been farming these 8 mu for 30 years. My husband and son work construction in Handan, so it's mostly me and my daughter-in-law doing the farm work. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those technical pamphlets much — I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

My main crop is cotton, 5 mu. That's what pays the bills. The other 3 mu I split into 2 mu spring maize and 1 mu mungbean — can't put all eggs in one basket, and the mungbean is good for family eating and some cash. 

For cotton, I'll plant in mid-April when the soil warms up. I buy improved seed from the shop, same kind as last year, costs about 30 yuan per mu. I rotary till the field first. At planting I put down compound fertilizer, about 25 kg per mu — that's roughly one bag for every two mu. Then when the cotton buds show in June, I topdress urea, about 10 kg per mu. At flowering I add another 10 kg. My neighbor Wang tried cutting back on fertilizer last year and his cotton was shorter with fewer bolls, so I'm not doing that. I don't know the exact nitrogen numbers, but it's about two bags of urea per mu total. I irrigate three times — budding, flowering, and boll setting. Water from the well costs electricity money, so I don't waste it, but dry cotton loses yield fast. I spray herbicide before planting and insecticide two or three times for bollworm. Cotton picking is the hard part — I do the early picks myself, but I hire three women from the village for the later picks, about 15 days total. That costs money, but my hands and back can't do it all, and if I miss a pick the cotton gets dirty and the price drops.

For the 2 mu maize, I plant late April with hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. One bag of compound at planting, then urea at jointing. Irrigate twice if no rain. One spray of herbicide. Family handles it between cotton tasks — doesn't need much watching.

The 1 mu mungbean goes in early May. Light tillage, one bag of compound, maybe water once if it's really dry. Easy crop, harvest in July. My daughter-in-law likes the mungbean soup, and we sell what we don't eat.

This year I'm spending about 3,000 yuan on inputs and hired labor. I have to be careful — my granddaughter starts school in September and we need cash for fees. So I'm doing about the same as last year. I'd rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad yield and have no money coming in. Last year was okay, no big drought or pest disaster, so I'll stick with what works.
